title: Grade 4 CREATIVE ARTS — Premium Revision Paper #11

pages.quiz:
CREATIVE ARTS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #11
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: CREATIVE ARTS
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. If the skin of a drum is loose, the sound is (1 mark)
   A. louder than a tight skin always
   B. the same as a tight skin
   C. lower
   D. higher

2. To improvise a rhythmic pattern means to (1 mark)
   A. write it before playing
   B. copy it from a book only
   C. stay silent
   D. make it up on the spot

3. Which is a non-melodic percussion instrument? (1 mark)
   A. Shaker
   B. Marimba
   C. Thumb piano
   D. Xylophone

4. When accompanying singers, the drummers should (1 mark)
   A. play softly enough for the singers to be heard
   B. stop at every line
   C. shout the words
   D. play as loud as possible

5. Which two positions are defenders that may enter the goal circle they defend? (1 mark)
   A. GS and C
   B. WA and C
   C. WD and WA
   D. GD and GK

6. Which attacker may NOT enter the goal circle? (1 mark)
   A. GA
   B. WA
   C. GS
   D. None

7. In an overhead pass, the ball starts (1 mark)
   A. above the head
   B. between the knees
   C. behind the knees
   D. at the ankles

8. Blue mixed with red makes (1 mark)
   A. green
   B. purple
   C. yellow
   D. orange

9. Overlapping in a montage means (1 mark)
   A. pieces are painted black
   B. one piece partly covers another
   C. pieces are cut into tiny bits
   D. pieces are far apart

10. Which of these letters has a tail below the baseline? (1 mark)
   A. l
   B. d
   C. y
   D. h

11. How long does one quaver last? (1 mark)
   A. Two beats
   B. A quarter of a beat only
   C. One beat
   D. Half a beat

12. A rhythmic pattern feels finished when it ends on (1 mark)
   A. a long note
   B. a rest
   C. a mistake
   D. a very short note

13. Hand signs for d, r and m are shown at heights that (1 mark)
   A. go up from d to r to m
   B. go down from d to m
   C. are random
   D. stay the same

14. What is the main purpose of hand signs when singing? (1 mark)
   A. To keep flies away
   B. To show the pitch of the notes
   C. To tell the time
   D. To count money

15. The sol-fa syllable r is pronounced (1 mark)
   A. ray
   B. roh
   C. rah
   D. ree

16. The middle stripe of the Kenyan flag is (1 mark)
   A. red
   B. black
   C. blue
   D. green

17. Why should the knees lift high when sprinting? (1 mark)
   A. To look funny
   B. To trip others
   C. To give a stronger, longer stride
   D. To slow down

18. Which should you remove before gymnastics? (1 mark)
   A. Your smile
   B. Your hair
   C. Watches and bracelets
   D. Your clothes

19. A side roll is also called a (1 mark)
   A. frog roll
   B. log roll
   C. star roll
   D. crab roll

20. If you finish a gymnastics session, what should you do? (1 mark)
   A. Leave mats on the floor
   B. Run around wildly
   C. Put equipment away and cool down
   D. Push the mats

21. In which direction should a side roll travel? (1 mark)
   A. Backwards over your head
   B. Round and round in place
   C. In a curve off the mat
   D. In a straight line along the mat

22. In this lesson's sequence, what comes after the crab balance? (1 mark)
   A. Netball pass
   B. Side roll immediately
   C. Lower the hips to the mat
   D. Sprint start

23. Which folk songs are sung when young people become adults in their community? (1 mark)
   A. Initiation songs
   B. Work songs
   C. Naming songs
   D. Topical songs

24. The East African Community is (1 mark)
   A. a group of countries in East Africa that work together
   B. a river
   C. a school
   D. a type of drum

25. In music, the sign p means (1 mark)
   A. stop
   B. loud
   C. soft
   D. fast

26. For a well-lit photograph of a person, the sun should be (1 mark)
   A. under the ground
   B. behind the person
   C. inside the lens
   D. behind the photographer

27. When you give feedback on a friend's photograph you should (1 mark)
   A. say nothing
   B. laugh
   C. say what you like first and then suggest one improvement
   D. say it is terrible

28. The word photography comes from words meaning (1 mark)
   A. writing with ink
   B. drawing with sound
   C. drawing with paint
   D. drawing with light

29. The descant recorder is played by (1 mark)
   A. blowing air into it
   B. shaking it
   C. plucking strings
   D. striking it

30. On the staff, the note G sits on (1 mark)
   A. line 3
   B. line 2
   C. the top line
   D. a space above the staff

31. Where should the mouthpiece rest? (1 mark)
   A. Between your lips, not your teeth
   B. On your chin
   C. Behind your ear
   D. Between your teeth

32. Where should a recorder be stored? (1 mark)
   A. On a hot windowsill
   B. In the mud
   C. Under a heavy load
   D. In its bag or box

33. How should you use steps or a ladder to enter? (1 mark)
   A. Go head first
   B. Ignore rails
   C. Face the steps, hold the rails and go feet first
   D. Jump onto them

34. A streamlined shape is (1 mark)
   A. long and thin like an arrow
   B. wide and floppy
   C. bent like a chair
   D. round like a ball

35. Which is a safe way to enter the pool? (1 mark)
   A. Head first from a run
   B. Being pushed
   C. Jumping onto others
   D. Feet first, watched by the teacher

36. A glide is (1 mark)
   A. a float on the back
   B. a dive
   C. moving through water after a push without kicking
   D. a fast kick

37. Which Kiswahili word means elephant? (1 mark)
   A. tembo
   B. twiga
   C. kuku
   D. nyoka

38. Who can teach you an indigenous game from your community? (1 mark)
   A. An elder
   B. A stranger online
   C. Only a computer
   D. Nobody

39. A working portfolio holds (1 mark)
   A. work in progress such as sketches and trials
   B. balls
   C. food
   D. only finished prize work

40. The message of an art work is (1 mark)
   A. what the artist wants us to learn or feel
   B. the artist's age
   C. the size of the frame
   D. the price

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Name two animal movement games. (2 marks)

42. Explain what overlapping is and why it is used in a montage. (3 marks)

43. What is a balance in gymnastics? (2 marks)

44. Describe the roles in a folk song performance. (4 marks)

45. Explain how a drum makes sound and how its parts work together. (5 marks)

46. Describe three qualities of a good rhythmic pattern. (3 marks)

47. How many beats are there in the pattern ta-te ta-te taa taa? Show your working. (3 marks)

48. Explain the difference between a sacred song and a patriotic song. (3 marks)

49. Why is it important to keep the right posture during a sprint? (3 marks)

50. Describe how to compose a short melody with d, r and m, and how to check that it is a good melody. (5 marks)

51. Why should you never point a camera directly at the sun? (3 marks)

52. Give three common mistakes in the crab balance and how to fix them. (3 marks)

53. Describe the procedure of making charcoal sticks for drawing, from cutting to cooling. (5 marks)

54. Give three reasons for flying the Kenyan flag at an athletics event. (3 marks)

55. What is the difference between tempo and dynamics? (2 marks)

56. Describe how to make an overhead pass. (3 marks)

57. State two ways to keep the working area clean after painting. (2 marks)

58. Write a melody that goes up by steps from d to m and comes down to d, and state the number of notes. (3 marks)

59. Describe how to make flour paste glue. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
CREATIVE ARTS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #11 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — lower
   A loose skin vibrates more slowly, so the sound is lower.

2. D — make it up on the spot
   Improvising is inventing a pattern without preparing it first.

3. A — Shaker
   A shaker gives a rattling sound but not different notes for a tune.

4. A — play softly enough for the singers to be heard
   Accompaniment supports the singers and must not cover their voices.

5. D — GD and GK
   The Goal Defence and the Goal Keeper may play in their defending circle.

6. B — WA
   The Wing Attack plays in the centre and goal thirds but not in the circle.

7. A — above the head
   The ball is lifted above the head before it is thrown.

8. B — purple
   Blue and red give purple.

9. B — one piece partly covers another
   Overlapping helps to fill gaps and make the montage full.

10. C — y
   The letter y has a tail below the baseline.

11. D — Half a beat
   A quaver is half a beat.

12. A — a long note
   Ending on a crotchet, a long note, makes it sound complete.

13. A — go up from d to r to m
   The signs rise as the pitch rises.

14. B — To show the pitch of the notes
   Hand signs help singers see and remember how high a note is.

15. A — ray
   The syllable r is ray.

16. A — red
   Red is the middle stripe.

17. C — To give a stronger, longer stride
   High knees produce a powerful stride.

18. C — Watches and bracelets
   Jewellery can hurt you or others.

19. B — log roll
   Keeping the body straight like a log gives it the name log roll.

20. C — Put equipment away and cool down
   Tidying and cooling down are good habits.

21. D — In a straight line along the mat
   Rolling in a straight line keeps you on the mat.

22. C — Lower the hips to the mat
   You lower the hips, lie straight, then roll.

23. A — Initiation songs
   Initiation songs mark the change from child to adult.

24. A — a group of countries in East Africa that work together
   The community brings countries together to cooperate.

25. C — soft
   The letter p stands for soft.

26. D — behind the photographer
   Light falls on the front of the subject.

27. C — say what you like first and then suggest one improvement
   Kind and helpful feedback works best.

28. D — drawing with light
   Photography means drawing with light.

29. A — blowing air into it
   A recorder is a wind instrument that you blow.

30. B — line 2
   G is on the second line from the bottom with the treble clef.

31. A — Between your lips, not your teeth
   Lips form the seal.

32. D — In its bag or box
   A case protects it.

33. C — Face the steps, hold the rails and go feet first
   Use the rails and enter carefully.

34. A — long and thin like an arrow
   A long shape slips easily through water.

35. D — Feet first, watched by the teacher
   Feet-first entry is safe.

36. C — moving through water after a push without kicking
   Gliding uses the momentum of the push.

37. A — tembo
   Tembo is an elephant.

38. A — An elder
   Elders know many traditional games.

39. A — work in progress such as sketches and trials
   It shows how work develops.

40. A — what the artist wants us to learn or feel
   The message is the idea communicated.

SECTION B
----
41. (2 marks)
   Answer: Frog jump, crab walk, elephant walk, snake slither, hare hop, crocodile crawl, giraffe stretch, monkey swing. Any two.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: Overlapping means placing one piece so it partly covers another. It removes gaps and makes the montage look full and joined up.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the meaning, 2 marks for the reasons.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: A position held still for a few seconds under control.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for still position, 1 mark for control or holding.

44. (4 marks)
   Answer: The soloist leads the song; the chorus answers or repeats; the instrumentalists play instruments to keep the beat; dancers move to the music.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each role.

45. (5 marks)
   Answer: The beater or hand strikes the drumhead, which vibrates and makes the sound. The hollow shell makes the sound fuller and louder. The ropes hold the skin tight, and a tighter skin gives a higher sound.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for striking, vibrating skin, shell, ropes, and effect of tightness on pitch.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: It has variation of note values, repetition of a group of notes and ends on a long note.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: 4 beats. Ta-te is 1 beat, ta-te is 1 beat, taa is 1 beat and taa is 1 beat, so 1+1+1+1 = 4.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct stage.

48. (3 marks)
   Answer: A sacred song is a song of worship that praises God. A patriotic song shows love for the country, such as the national anthem.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning, 1 mark for an example.

49. (3 marks)
   Answer: It keeps the body moving forward in a straight line. It saves energy and helps speed. It prevents pain or injury.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid reason.

50. (5 marks)
   Answer: Choose a rhythm. Give each note a syllable, using steps. End on d. Sing it with hand signs. Check that it has variation and stepwise motion and that it ends on d.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of five valid points.

51. (3 marks)
   Answer: It can hurt your eyes and the strong light will spoil the picture.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for eyes, 1 mark for picture, 1 mark for explanation.

52. (3 marks)
   Answer: Hips sagging: push harder. Bent arms: straighten them. Head dropped: keep it in line.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each mistake with a fix.

53. (5 marks)
   Answer: Cut dry, straight twigs about the length of a hand. Trim off bark, knots and leaves. Pack the twigs tightly in a tin and close the lid with a small hole. An adult burns the tin in a fire until the smoke stops. Leave the tin closed to cool completely before opening.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for cutting, trimming, packing, burning by an adult, and cooling.

54. (3 marks)
   Answer: It shows which country the athletes represent; it builds pride and patriotism; it brings people together to cheer; it shows respect to visitors. Any three.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

55. (2 marks)
   Answer: Tempo is the speed of the music. Dynamics are how loud or soft the music is.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

56. (3 marks)
   Answer: Lift the ball above the head with both hands and elbows slightly bent. Step forward and throw from behind the head, flicking wrists and fingers so the ball goes over the defender.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the start, 1 mark for the throw, 1 mark for going over the defender.

57. (2 marks)
   Answer: Wash the brushes and containers, wipe the desk, put the paper in the bin. Any two.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

58. (3 marks)
   Answer: d r m r d. There are five notes.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for going up, 1 mark for coming down, 1 mark for five.

59. (3 marks)
   Answer: Mix flour with a little cold water to a smooth paste. An adult adds hot water while stirring. Let it cool before use.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.
